question: Do the apologies show what Ibn Turka actually believed (an orthodox Sunni Sufi)?
proposition: Leonard Lewisohn, as Melvin-Koushki reports him, takes the apologies at face value and so presents Ibn Turka as an orthodox Sunni Sufi thinker.
scholar: Leonard Lewisohn (as reported by Melvin-Koushki; Lewisohn's own text was not read)
reasoning: MK says Lewisohn insists on taking the apologies at face value (pp.66, 77 of his article) and misrepresents Ibn Turka as an orthodox Sunni Sufi thinker.
MK calls the insistence ‘well-taken’ in one place and ‘misrepresenting’ in another, and answers that the oeuvre and the duress make face value impossible.
Everything here is at second hand through MK; the article itself was not opened.
